title: deferred-capture-liveness-and-kv-alignment-to-reduce-cudagraph-warmup-regressions
author: Asha Iyer
release_notes: Reduced CUDA-graph warmup token regression by introducing deferred capture + KV-cache alignment. Improves p50 tail during steady-state by up to 12% in mixed batch workloads. No API changes.
description:
Motivation: We observed several regressions in production and in perf canaries where CUDA-graph capture/replay would cause large warmup token penalties when requests arrived with partially-populated KV caches or when continuous-batching created fragmented shapes. This PR introduces a conservative, deferred-capture strategy plus KV-cache alignment heuristics and scheduler adjustments to avoid capturing graphs too early and to stitch kernels deterministically when replay shape variance is detected.

What this PR does (single-line description): Implement deferred graph capture, liveness-aware shape relaxation, and KV-cache alignment heuristics to reduce warmup regressions and stabilize replay in continuous-batching scenarios.

Key changes (high-level):
- runtime/cudagraphs/deferred_capture.cc: new coordinator that postpones final capture until a stable probe window has validated KV-cache priming and stable sequence-length distribution.
- runtime/scheduler/token_priority.h/.cc: add token-aware scheduling to prefer priming requests for probes and ensure priming work doesn't evict hot entries.
- runtime/kvcache/alignment.h/.cc: heuristics to align batch KV cache offsets across requests and to optionally inject short-priming micro-requests before capture.
- runtime/cudagraphs/kernel_stitcher.cc: kernel stitching path to merge a deterministic set of kernels when replay shapes differ slightly (relaxed shape guards).
- tests/ci/deterministic_replay_test.cpp: new deterministic replay tests and a CI-mode warmup benchmark that runs in the matrix.
- docs/observability/cudagraphs.md: documentation on telemetry emitted for deferred-capture decisions and warmup counters.

Design notes:
- Deferred capture: Instead of capturing as soon as a request first traverses the runtime, we now start in PROBE mode. PROBE gathers a small window of live requests (configurable, default 8 contiguous priming tokens) to validate the KV-cache priming state and sequence-length distribution. Only when the coordinator sees stable metrics (low shape variance, >75% requests with aligned KV offsets) does it perform final capture. This reduces captures that only see cold KV caches or fragmented batches.
- KV alignment: For workloads that routinely put different KV offsets into the same batch (e.g., mixing chat turns with and without prior context), we introduce alignment: small, cheap prefix priming (a short run that populates KV entries) before capture or replay. The alignment is conservative (default off for small models) and can be toggled by model profile.
- Liveness-based shape relaxation: Instead of strict shape guards that force fallback for any mismatch, we compute a liveness score and allow relaxed stitching for low-risk differences (e.g., a few tokens difference at tail). This is implemented as a deterministic kernel-stitch path that merges replayed kernels to match the observed shape while preserving replay safety.
- Scheduling: Token-priority scheduler ensures priming/probe requests are scheduled with slight priority so they can complete and stabilize the capture coordinator without causing large throughput regressions.

Benchmarks:
- Mixed-chat benchmark (50% cold-contex, 50% warm-context), p50 latency improved 8-12% post-merge across GPUs (A100, H100) at 32 concurrent streams. Warmup token count reduced from median 48->10 for probe-enabled captures.
- Continuous-batching stress: 99th percentile stable; failure/replay incidences decreased from 4.7% of captures to 0.6% over 24h of synthetic traffic.

Testing and CI:
- Added deterministic replay tests to ensure reproducible capture/replay on CI GPUs; these run in the night matrix and are fast-mode for PRs.
- Added local perf harness scripts used for the benchmark numbers.
- CI initially failed on an unrelated linter (long line in docs) — fixed in follow-up commit.

Risk and rollout:
- Default config is conservative and off for small models; rollout plan: enable PROBE mode by default for models listed in model-profiles/perf.json and monitor telemetry (deferred_capture.* metrics).
- Rollback: feature gated via runtime flag (--cudagraph-deferred-capture=false) and model profile entries; metrics emit a non-impacting trace to trace capture decisions.

Follow-ups:
- Integrate with autoscaler to consider priming load when scaling up dedicated pools.
- Telemetry-driven automatic tuning (future PR) to adjust probe window size per model.

Related work: references to prior PLs and tickets included in commits and Linear tasks ENG-1842 (capture regressions) and ENG-1908 (kv cache stability).

Commits summary: This is a squash PR that landed the following work in pieces: initial coordinator prototype, kernel-stitcher, KV alignment heuristics, scheduler changes, tests, and docs.

Files changed (high-level):
- runtime/cudagraphs/* (coordinator, stitcher, probes): ~450 additions, ~110 deletions
- runtime/kvcache/* (alignment): ~220 additions, ~45 deletions
- runtime/scheduler/* (priority logic): ~120 additions, ~30 deletions
- tests/ci/* (deterministic replay + perf harness): ~90 additions
- docs/observability/cudagraphs.md: ~60 additions

Review conversation (highlights):
- Miguel Santos (reviewer): "Great approach. My primary concern is ensuring we don't introduce head-of-line blocking due to probe priming. Can we cap the priming runtime and ensure probes are opportunistic?"
- Asha Iyer (author): "Answered: probes are capped to 8 priming tokens by default and the scheduler will make priming requests low-impact (token-priority with backoff). Added tests to simulate backpressure."
- Priya Kapoor (reviewer): "Please add a telemetry counter for 'probe_rejections' so we can see when alignment is skipped due to low coverage."
- Asha Iyer: "Added probe_rejections counter and dashboard snippet in docs. Also added an e2e test that asserts counter increments on synthetic misalignment."
- Evan Liu (approver): "Verified perf numbers in local harness on H100; approving pending CI green."
- CI: initial build failed on clang-format; rerun fixed by formatting commit. Final CI matrix: linux/cpp: pass, linux/python: pass, night/perf: pass.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals and green CI. Merged by Asha Iyer.

Notes for on-call / SRE: If you see increased priming load causing capacity pressure, the temporary mitigation is to toggle --cudagraph-deferred-capture=false for the affected pool or reduce model-profile probe window to 2. Telemetry keys: deferred_capture.probes, deferred_capture.captures, deferred_capture.probe_rejections, kv_alignment.injected_priming.
